edit frontend or data-ingestion behavior without running the listed smoke commands

Run service-router tests and at least py_compile for backend/app.py.

change expression validation, topology, or final result handling

Keep NetworkX optional and do not make execution topology depend on DOT export support.

edit Vite proxy or package dependencies

pitfalls.title: frontend_managed_external_api_tokens_must_remain_local_private_and_redacted
symptoms: A data ingestion script contains a hardcoded third-party API token value.
A future agent quotes token values in summaries, logs, or routing memory.
A Token configuration endpoint returns the submitted value or persists it in task state.
Tushare integration reads the legacy process environment instead of the frontend-managed local credential.
Calling tushare.set_token writes an extra tk.csv credential file in the user's home directory.
trigger_actions: edit data ingestion scripts
summarize config or token handling
add logs around external API calls
prepare commits touching data scripts
check_before_edit: Do not copy or quote token literal values.
Persist the frontend-supplied Token only in the ignored data/.tushare_token file with 0600 permissions and atomic replacement.
Never return the Token, put it in command arguments or persisted job state, or allow changes while the refresh lock is held.
Keep config.require_tushare_token on the same local credential file and explicitly ignore legacy TUSHARE_TOKEN environment values.
Pass the frontend-managed Token directly to tushare.pro_api(token); do not call tushare.set_token or create a second home-directory credential file.

pitfalls.title: cli_and_web_refresh_share_a_filesystem_lock_and_atomic_promotion_contract
symptoms: CLI and Web jobs run simultaneously because they do not use the same lock file on the same local filesystem.
A public production deployment exposes a write endpoint without an explicit enable decision.
Full-refresh files become visible before read-only validation and atomic manifest activation complete.
A successful Tushare fetch is repeated because local snapshot post-processing failed.
Late or revised observations are skipped because incremental overlap rows do not replace matching stored keys.
Incremental merge mixes string or integer stored dates with Timestamp values and Arrow conversion fails before schema alignment.
Independent worker limiters or worker-side Parquet writes exceed the account quota or expose partially merged data.
An empty or identical incremental window rewrites a multi-gigabyte Parquet file and rebuilds the complete analytics snapshot even though no observable data changed.
A Web-started refresh loses its supervising process during an API restart and is later surfaced only as a generic interrupted job, even though already-landed files remain reusable.
A multi-gigabyte streaming merge performs real work but emits no stdout for longer than the idle timeout, so the supervisor can mistake it for a stalled child.
trigger_actions: enable DATA_REFRESH_ENABLED in production
change refresh lock, persisted state, heartbeat, subprocess logging, or timeout behavior
change full-refresh staging, validation, or manifest activation
change date overlap, merge precedence, checkpoint, empty response, or atomic write behavior
change refresh worker count, request frequency, or date/code thread-pool scheduling
check_before_edit: Keep production refresh disabled unless the deployment protects the endpoint.
Keep CLI, Web, and local snapshot rebuild on the same non-blocking filesystem lock; preserve inherited child ownership and persisted heartbeat/state.

Stream a bounded, redacted log tail instead of capture_output, retain checkpoints after interruption, and expose persisted modules/scopes as a safe one-click retry contract when the supervising API process is lost.
Long local Parquet merges must emit flushed progress often enough to refresh the supervisor's activity timer; do not treat a silent CPU-bound merge as idle.
Write full refreshes to an isolated version, build the local metrics snapshot, validate it, and atomically switch the manifest; keep the old manifest on any failure.
Treat analytics rebuild or promotion failure as a warning after successful fetching so operators can rebuild locally without another Tushare call.
Refetch the configured trading-day overlap and let incoming rows replace matching keys while preserving atomic sorted output.
Normalize date values before deduplication, then serialize them back to the existing Parquet Arrow date-column type before conversion and atomic replacement.

Make every worker share one thread-safe RateLimiter and retry policy; keep pagination sequential within each date and perform checkpoint or final Parquet writes only after worker results return to the coordinator.

Copy untouched instrument groups in Arrow, preserve the original Parquet when the merged content is identical, and reuse a non-stale analytics snapshot only when every analytics source fingerprint is unchanged.

pitfalls.title: all_tushare_readers_must_resolve_one_validated_active_snapshot
symptoms: One reader bypasses resolve_tushare_data_dir or resolve_market_data_file and serves legacy data while other readers use the active version.
An invalid manifest or operator override escapes the project data boundary or silently points at an incomplete directory.
A parquet file changes after validation but before activation, making the validation report stale.
A full candidate replaces the active manifest even though a required ETF, fund, calendar, or analytics file is absent.
trigger_actions: add or change any Tushare-backed reader
change TUSHARE_DATA_DIR or active-manifest handling
change snapshot validation, activation, or required-file inventory
change full-refresh promotion or rollback
blast_radius: all Tushare-backed APIs and research calculations
check_before_edit: Resolve the active version at operation time and use the legacy data root only when no valid manifest exists or a documented compatibility fallback applies.
Keep snapshot directories inside the data root and require every core ETF, fund, calendar, and analytics file before activation.
Bind activation to a passed validation report for the same directory and recheck each required file size and mtime before replacing the manifest.
Use atomic JSON replacement and keep the previous manifest untouched on validation, inventory, or write failure.

pitfalls.title: dashboard_analytics_preserve_share_class_date_and_missing_metric_semantics
symptoms: A Dashboard request opens the complete NAV or candle history instead of info tables, parquet metadata, and the metrics snapshot.
ETF list_date and public-fund found_date are merged into one ambiguous trend or current AUM is inferred from disclosed issue_amount.
A short-history or stale share class ranks with a zero metric or stale value rather than null/exclusion.
A product that does not cover the complete selected interval is still ranked, or a discontinuous adjusted NAV creates implausible return and volatility values.
ETF price/NAV premium is calculated from adjusted NAV instead of same-date unit_nav.
Partial fund or snapshot availability makes the whole Dashboard unavailable instead of degrading only affected sections.
trigger_actions: edit instrument analytics summaries, trends, rankings, or snapshot builder
edit Dashboard data hooks, scope tabs, cards, charts, or ranking tables
change metric definitions, observation thresholds, freshness rules, or status_code lifecycle mapping
change ETF premium/liquidity calculations
check_before_edit: Keep request paths on cached info tables, parquet metadata, and instrument_metrics_snapshot; stream full history only in the local builder or validator.
Count each (instrument_type, ts_code) share class independently, keep ETF list_date and fund found_date series separate, and never combine issue_amount across kinds.

Use adj_nav for common performance, require the product to cover the complete selected interval, reject adjusted-NAV discontinuities using unit_nav or accum_nav as a reference, and preserve quality failures as null or ranking exclusion.
Return complete, partial, or unavailable per available section so one missing kind or snapshot does not erase the other kind's structure data.

pitfalls.title: typed_v22_axes_semantics_version_pairs_and_njit_kernels_are_context_bound
symptoms: A typed-v2.2 change edits or reinterprets persisted typed 2.0, typed 2.1, or legacy v1 indicator definitions in place.
A time series, asset vector, or time-asset matrix is combined through implicit positional broadcasting.
Values with incompatible semantic dimensions or price bases are accepted by additive/comparison operators, or a numeric tensor is accepted where a bool mask is required.
Public operator parameters, mask shapes, or overload names drift from the versioned signatures consumed by the guided builder.
A DSL 2.0 definition runs against a 2.1 operator registry, or a saved 2.1 definition advertises a variable/data/context protocol version that is not installed.
A product formula accepts portfolio-only variables, or a portfolio formula silently uses a single-product-only variable.
The public compose/infer/validate/evaluate-portfolio payload drifts from the typed service, or portfolio evaluation is detached from an immutable run snapshot.
A public or canonical operator lacks a warmed fixed-signature KernelSpec, or production evaluation silently calls a Python operator fallback.
trigger_actions: edit typed_types, typed_operators, typed_dsl, or typed_service
edit variable_registry or public typed meta
add typed-v2.2 composition/inference routes or KernelSpec signatures
add portfolio custom indicator evaluation
migrate legacy indicator definitions
blast_radius: public variable/operator metadata and guided composition
check_before_edit: Keep typed-v2.2, typed-v2.1, typed-v2.0, and persisted legacy v1 definitions separate; adapt execution plans without rewriting historical formulas.
Require exact nominal axes unless a documented operator explicitly supports scalar broadcast.
Require compatible semantic dimensions and price bases for additive/comparison operations, and preserve bool-mask dtype and mask signatures through public metadata.
Keep executable expression source separate from display_latex; render code identifiers only after escaping text and use canonical variable symbols with text-style subscripts.
Pair each saved DSL version with its installed operator/variable/data/context versions; keep business indicator formulas out of the public pure-mathematics operator catalog.
Validate context requirements before evaluation; portfolio formulas must run only against an immutable portfolio-run snapshot through evaluate-portfolio.
Require 97/97 canonical and 92/92 public KernelSpec coverage, successful startup warmup, python_fallback=0, and python_operator_calls=0.
Run typed type, catalog, compiler, NJIT kernel, runtime, and product-service tests together.

Persist decision_date and effective_date, and apply a decision only on the next common data day.
Keep run snapshots append-only and reject target deletion while a snapshot references it.
Keep product rankings and portfolio research targets separate; normalize warning.message and weight paths in the frontend client.

pitfalls.title: custom_indicator_results_depend_on_real_series_windows_and_locked_revisions
symptoms: A missing parquet file silently falls back to simulated prices or a zero-valued metric.
1W or calendar-month/year windows use a different boundary rule across preview, detail, comparison, and ranking.
A conditional Tushare variable is offered without checking the selected product, period, and historical as-of date, or an availability-service failure is treated as available.
An indicator is rejected only because its catalog product-kind hint differs, without checking the formula's actual required fields for that product.
An existing indicator is inserted by mutable ID or copied from stale client state instead of being resolved and checked by locked revision and matching protocol versions.
The headline LaTeX expands rolling-window loops, missing-value branches, or recursive implementation details instead of using compact mathematical operator symbols.
A fund NAV field is exposed for a historical as-of date before its announcement date, or partial field coverage is silently treated as complete.
An update or delete omits revision, or a saved plan runs the latest indicator instead of its locked historical version.
A product with any missing selected metric is normalized as zero and included in ranking.
trigger_actions: edit custom indicator CRUD, evaluate, or plan routes
edit variable registry, availability API, series provider, or period selection
edit JSON persistence, cache keys, or invalidation
edit IndicatorStudio variable catalog or guided operator parameters
add existing-indicator composition or formula reuse
edit typed mathematical LaTeX or time-series formula previews
edit detail, comparison, or evaluation-plan indicator integration
blast_radius: guided formula inputs and historical availability
check_before_edit: Use real or fixture parquet only; missing data must return null plus a warning.
Keep 1W at five return observations and calendar M/Y windows anchored by the latest observation before the boundary.
Resolve variable availability for every selected product, period, and as-of date; fail closed in both the catalog and operator parameter drawer when all relevant targets fail.
Treat applicable_product_kinds as a catalog hint only; compile required_variables and report source, field, observation, coverage, or common-window blockers per product before calculation.

Resolve inserted indicators by indicator_id plus revision on the server, require matching context and DSL/registry/data/schema versions, and expand to an independent scalar expression rather than a mutable runtime reference.

When lifting a scalar indicator into a rolling series, lock the source revision and definition hash, expand supported reductions at definition time, keep the window as a formula constant, and fail closed for unsupported window-level context or reductions.

Keep the headline formula semantic and compact: use symbols such as mu, sigma, s, windowed min/max, smoothing S, or drawdown D; keep min_periods, NaN branches and implementation recurrences in the detailed DAG explanation.
Respect ann_date <= as_of for reported NAV fields and surface partial coverage instead of silently filling or claiming full availability.
Require revision for every mutable update/delete and run plans against locked indicator revisions.
Exclude products missing any selected metric from ranking instead of treating missing values as zero.

pitfalls.title: metric_values_require_locked_presentation_and_explicit_unavailable_states
symptoms: The same raw indicator value is rendered with different scaling, precision, or unit across detail, comparison, evaluation, and portfolio pages.
A frontend infers percent or currency formatting from an indicator name instead of MetricPresentation.
A missing, insufficient, failed, or inapplicable result is displayed as zero or loses its stable reason code.
A historical evaluation result is formatted by looking up the latest catalog revision rather than using the locked presentation embedded in the result.
A selector hides an indicator only from a static ETF/fund label, or shows it without explaining which selected products lack the required fields.
localStorage persists products, results, or historical as-of values instead of only indicator IDs and the runtime period.
trigger_actions: edit MetricPresentation construction or evaluate result payloads
edit shared metric selectors, value/status components, or browser preferences
edit product research, detail, comparison, evaluation-plan, dashboard, or portfolio metric displays
blast_radius: cross-page indicator selection and browser defaults
check_before_edit: Embed the locked MetricPresentation in every evaluation result and use it directly in frontend rendering.
Keep value_scale, display_format, precision, unit, notation, direction, version, and applicability explicit; never infer them from display names.
Render null as an explicit unavailable state with warnings and never coerce it to zero or include it in ranking.

Filter selectors by calculation context, keep field-dependent indicators visible, and use per-product input requirements to explain full or partial runtime availability while preserving hidden compatibility definitions for historical locked runs.
Keep indicator-display:v1 preferences limited to valid indicator IDs and runtime period.

pitfalls.title: indicator_batch_workers_require_generation_bound_arrays_and_single_owner_cleanup
symptoms: One evaluation plan rereads the same Parquet source for each metric or period.
Worker tasks serialize NumPy payloads instead of passing shared-memory or mmap descriptors and integer window bounds.
A data refresh reuses cached arrays or windows from an older snapshot generation.
Multiple Uvicorn workers each create a process pool, or BLAS and Numba threads multiply process-level concurrency.
Timeout, cancellation, worker failure, or service restart leaves shared arrays or mmap files behind.
A request performs first-use Numba compilation instead of using lifespan-prewarmed fixed signatures.
A snapshot shortcut removes only part of a saved evaluation-plan fused batch, creating an unsaved subset shape that misses the startup-warmed immutable batch plan.
Large paged results outlive their bounded TTL or return an unstable missing/expired contract.
trigger_actions: edit indicator batch loading, window caching, fused kernels, process scheduling, or scoring
edit shared-memory, mmap, worker lifespan, timeout, or admission logic
edit evaluation-plan result pagination, retention, or execution metadata
change Docker worker, shm, BLAS, Numba, or indicator cache configuration
blast_radius: API process availability and CPU saturation
temporary shared resources and paged result retention
check_before_edit: Resolve locked formulas and physical dependencies once, scan each required Parquet source once, and key data/window/result caches by active data generation.
Pass only shared-memory or mmap descriptors and numeric plans to workers; keep strings and presentation assembly in the API process.
Use one Uvicorn worker per container, prewarm fixed Numba signatures in lifespan workers, and cap BLAS, process, and Numba concurrency with CPU tokens.

Preserve saved fused-batch membership at runtime: snapshot reuse may skip a fused group only when the whole group and all targets are covered; partial snapshot hits must execute the original warmed batch instead of constructing a new subset shape.
Keep parent ownership of unlink, terminate failed workers before shared cleanup, and remove only protected orphan resources whose owner PID is gone.
Keep result-cache TTL, 410 RESULT_EXPIRED, page bounds, and Retry-After busy responses stable.
